role_description: Researches and qualifies enterprise prospects, runs multi-channel outbound, books qualified discovery meetings and maintains CRM hygiene.
paper_title: Sales Development Representative (SDR) – Enterprise Sales | Assessment Paper

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the strongest definition of an Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) for enterprise outbound?
options: Any company large enough to afford the product.
A firmographic and behavioural description of accounts that get the most value and close fastest — industry, size, tech stack, business trigger and buying-team shape.
The job titles the SDR finds easiest to reach on LinkedIn.
The list of accounts the marketing team has already run ads against.

questions.question_text: A prospect replies to a cold email: "Interesting, but we're heads-down until next quarter." What is the most effective SDR response?
options: Mark the lead as closed-lost and move on.
Acknowledge the timing, ask one question about what changes next quarter, and propose a short call now to be ready — with a specific dated fallback if they prefer to wait.
Send the same pitch again the following morning.
Reply asking them to forward you to whoever is not busy.

questions.question_text: In a qualification framework such as MEDDIC, what does identifying the "Economic Buyer" specifically require?
options: Finding the most senior person listed on the company website.
Confirming who holds discretionary budget authority to approve this purchase and how they make that decision.
Confirming the name of the procurement software the company uses.
Identifying which competitor the prospect currently pays.

questions.question_text: Which CRM practice most directly protects enterprise pipeline quality in an SDR team?
options: Logging every activity and next step against the correct account and contact, with accurate disposition and a dated next action.
Creating a new lead record for each email sent to maximise activity counts.
Leaving notes in a personal spreadsheet so the CRM stays uncluttered.
Marking all engaged prospects as Qualified so Account Executives see more pipeline.

questions.question_text: You are given a territory of 300 enterprise accounts (2,000+ employees, financial services and insurance) and asked to build a prioritised target list of 40 accounts for this quarter. Describe your research method: what signals you would look for, what sources you would use, and how you would rank the accounts.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Be concrete about signals and sources, and explain your ranking logic.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers define ICP fit criteria plus intent/trigger signals: recent funding or M&A, leadership hires in relevant functions, job postings revealing tooling or initiatives, earnings-call and annual-report priorities, regulatory pressure, tech-stack evidence, existing customer lookalikes, product usage or web/content engagement, past closed-lost revisits. Sources: LinkedIn/Sales Navigator, company filings and investor material, job boards, news, review sites, CRM history, intent data, internal customer references. Ranking should combine fit + trigger + accessibility (warm paths, existing champions who changed jobs) into a tiered A/B/C model with a stated weighting and a plan for how many contacts per account to multi-thread. Deduct for list-buying only, no signals, or no prioritisation logic.

questions.question_text: Write an actual cold email to a VP of Customer Operations at a large insurance company, plus the LinkedIn message you would send the same person. Then explain the reasoning behind your choices.
questions.instructions: Write the real copy (subject line and body), keep the email under 150 words, then add a short rationale. Total 250-400 words.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Assess the copy itself: specific and credible subject line; opening that references a researched trigger about that company rather than generic flattery; a clearly stated problem in the prospect's language; brief evidence or peer proof point; one low-friction ask; no multi-paragraph feature dump; correct tone for a VP; mobile-readable length. LinkedIn message should be shorter, non-duplicative and conversational. Rationale should explain personalisation source, the single hypothesis being tested, why the CTA is low-friction, and how it fits a multi-touch sequence. Deduct heavily for template-filler personalisation ('I loved your post'), feature lists, multiple asks, or copy that could be sent to any company unchanged.

questions.question_text: You get a prospect on the phone and have roughly six minutes. Write the discovery questions you would ask to decide whether to book a meeting for an Account Executive, and state exactly what you must learn before you consider the lead qualified.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. List the actual questions and your qualification bar.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers open with permission and a crisp reason for the call, then probe current process and pain, quantified impact, who else is affected, what they have tried, timing/compelling event, decision process and who would need to be involved, and budget ownership at a high level. Should state an explicit qualification bar (e.g. fit to ICP + acknowledged problem + relevant stakeholder + plausible timeline) and what would disqualify or nurture instead. Credit for listening-led phrasing, avoiding a pitch, confirming the next step with a specific date/time and sending a recap with attendees and agenda. Deduct for pitching, only asking about budget, or no stated qualification threshold.

questions.question_text: Your booked-meeting rate has dropped for three consecutive weeks and two of your last four booked meetings were no-shows. Describe how you would diagnose and fix this, and how you would manage your follow-up and CRM discipline to prevent it recurring.
questions.instructions: Write 250-400 words. Show the diagnostic path and the concrete corrective actions.
questions.evaluation_criteria: Strong answers work funnel metrics stage by stage — list quality/ICP drift, deliverability and open rates, reply and positive-reply rates, connect rates by time of day, sequence step performance, messaging fatigue, competitor noise — and test one variable at a time. No-show fixes: confirmations, calendar invite with agenda and value, reminder cadence, booking closer to the call date, qualifying the attendee's authority and genuine interest, pre-call research shared in advance. Prevention: disciplined task/next-step management in CRM, accurate dispositions, defined follow-up cadence and time-blocking, weekly self-review of metrics, asking for coaching and reviewing call recordings. Deduct for answers that only say 'send more emails' or blame the list without a diagnostic method.
